Art

Ten paintings from the last year or so. Mostly about telling the difference between what is performed and what is real.

10 plates

Respect works like a pyramid scheme. Perform it long enough and eventually you are allowed to stop earning it. My first painting that I really committed to finishing. I will leave the rest unsaid.

Painted from the view off my balcony last summer, in a purple shade of my favorite sunglasses. The title borrows a line from Rosa Anschütz. I do not need anyone to perform for me. I already see who they are.

For the people I met who had started talking like their favorite influencers instead of themselves. I would rather know someone messy and real than another copy of something viral.

A reminder that nothing is quite as important as it feels. A little hedonism, and a little fear of letting go completely.

Painted in the middle of the hardest year I have had. Waiting on a process that kept moving its own goalposts, working every day, and eventually walking away from a job I loved because staying still had become its own kind of cost. Not a success story. Just a trade I was willing to make.

For every conversation about a plan that starts once some approval finally comes through. Life does not wait for the paperwork. Nothing rationalizes postponing what you actually want to do.

Four out of five. That is all I will say about this one.

A place I visit often lately. Headphones on, mind circling the same questions, nodding along to the rhythm without needing the questions to resolve. Some loops you do not escape. You just learn to move inside them.

An abstract fish, painted from leftover paint. She is missing a fin and does not move much, but the current still carries her where she needs to go. She is aware, and she has let go.

One snap of the fingers, and the way I see something changes completely. Perspective is the whole trick.

Portfolio

Six CAD and simulation projects: motorsport concepts, a SpaceX tribute, and architectural drafting. Modeled in SolidWorks and AutoCAD, simulated in ANSYS.

06 selected
Concept designSolidWorks

Aerodynamic Helmet Concept

A motorsport-inspired helmet modeled in SolidWorks, built around smooth aerodynamic contours and detailed surface work, a study in blending performance with style.

Reverse engineeringSolidWorks

Dragon Crew Capsule

Built from reference photos using a visual reverse-engineering approach, this SolidWorks model captures the capsule's aerodynamic form and structural detail, a tribute to SpaceX's spacecraft.

Product designSolidWorks

The Board

A custom skateboard assembly modeled entirely from scratch. Pastel tones and wood textures keep it playful and clean, while a Banksy quote on the grip tape adds a rebellious touch.

Product designSolidWorks

The Bottle

Smooth, sculptural lines meet bold diamond-pattern grips and glowing cyan highlights. The number 21 is a quiet nod to Vector Racing, a team I helped found.

Architectural draftingAutoCAD

Wooden Bungalow

A compact bungalow drafted in AutoCAD with detailed floor plans and elevations, designed with functionality and simplicity in mind.

SimulationANSYS Fluent

CFD Analysis

Velocity contours and CO₂ dispersion studies for a land development and an underground car park fire scenario, simulating wind loads, flow behavior, and jet-fan performance.
